questions.prompt: She wants to buy ___ new car.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' before a singular countable noun starting with a consonant sound when introduced for the first time.

questions.prompt: He ate ___ apple after lunch.
questions.explanation: Use 'an' before a singular countable noun starting with a vowel sound ('apple').

questions.prompt: It takes about ___ hour to drive to the city center.
questions.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a silent 'h', so it starts with a vowel sound (/aʊər/), requiring 'an'.

questions.prompt: She goes to ___ university in London.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a consonant sound (/j/), so it takes 'a', not 'an'.

questions.prompt: My uncle is ___ honest man.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' starts with a silent 'h', creating a vowel sound (/ɒnɪst/), which requires 'an'.

questions.prompt: They spotted ___ UFO in the night sky.
questions.explanation: 'UFO' is pronounced starting with the consonant sound /j/ ('you-ef-oh'), so 'a' is correct.

questions.prompt: France is ___ European country.
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with the consonant sound /j/ ('yoo-ruh-pee-uhn'), requiring 'a'.

questions.prompt: He is studying to become ___ engineer.
questions.explanation: 'Engineer' starts with a vowel sound (/ɛndʒɪnɪər/), requiring 'an'.

questions.prompt: We stayed at ___ hotel near the beach.
questions.explanation: 'Hotel' starts with a sounded 'h' consonant sound in modern English, taking 'a'.

questions.prompt: She has ___ unique style of painting.
questions.explanation: 'Unique' begins with the consonant sound /j/ ('yoo-neek'), so it uses 'a'.

questions.prompt: I need ___ one-dollar bill for the vending machine.
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/ ('wun'), taking 'a'.

questions.prompt: He received ___ MBA degree last year.
questions.explanation: The abbreviation 'MBA' is pronounced starting with a vowel sound ('em-bee-ay'), so it uses 'an'.

questions.prompt: Is there ___ ATM near here?
questions.explanation: 'ATM' starts with the vowel sound 'ay' (/eɪ/), requiring 'an'.

questions.prompt: She bought ___ house with a large garden.
questions.explanation: 'House' begins with the consonant sound /h/, taking 'a'.

questions.prompt: He works as ___ accountant for a law firm.
questions.explanation: 'Accountant' starts with a vowel sound, requiring 'an'.

questions.prompt: Look at ___ moon tonight; it is so bright.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' with unique natural objects like the sun, moon, and Earth.

questions.prompt: She is ___ tallest student in our class.
questions.explanation: Superlative adjectives ('tallest') always require the definite article 'the'.

questions.prompt: I found a dog. ___ dog was very friendly.
questions.explanation: When referencing a noun for the second time, it becomes specific and requires 'the'.

questions.prompt: This is ___ first time I have visited Paris.
questions.explanation: Ordinal numbers ('first', 'second', 'third') take 'the'.

questions.prompt: They went on a cruise across ___ Atlantic Ocean.
questions.explanation: Names of oceans, seas, and rivers require 'the'.

questions.prompt: ___ president of the committee opened the meeting.
questions.explanation: Specific roles or titles that are unique in a given context take 'the'.

revision.reason: Zero article is also standard after 'elected' ('He was elected president'). Rewrote the prompt so the unique role is the subject and needs 'the'.

questions.prompt: The government should do more to help ___ poor.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' + adjective to refer to a specific group of people as a collective whole.

questions.prompt: We hiked across ___ Alps during our vacation.
questions.explanation: Mountain ranges (plural) take 'the', whereas individual peak names do not.

questions.prompt: She lives in ___ Netherlands.
questions.explanation: Plural country names or countries with political structures in their name take 'the'.

questions.prompt: Can you pass me ___ salt on the table?
questions.explanation: The salt is specific because it is located right on the table in front of both speaker and listener.

questions.prompt: ___ Amazon is the largest river by discharge volume.
questions.explanation: Rivers take the definite article 'the'.

questions.prompt: Who was ___ last person to leave the room?
questions.explanation: Words indicating sequence or uniqueness like 'last' require 'the'.

questions.prompt: ___ French are famous for their rich culinary traditions.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' before nationality adjectives to refer to the nation's people as a whole.

questions.prompt: Turn off ___ lights when you leave.
questions.explanation: Refers to the specific lights in the current room/context.

questions.prompt: ___ Earth revolves around the sun.
questions.explanation: Unique astronomical bodies in general contexts take 'the'.

questions.prompt: ___ water is essential for human survival.
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns used in a general sense take no article.

questions.prompt: ___ dogs are known to be loyal companions.
questions.explanation: Plural countable nouns used to make general statements take no article.

questions.prompt: I am learning to speak ___ Spanish.
questions.explanation: Languages take no article unless followed by the word 'language' (e.g., the Spanish language).

questions.prompt: She moved to ___ Haiti two years ago.
questions.explanation: Most singular country names take no article.

questions.prompt: We usually eat ___ dinner at 7:00 PM.
questions.explanation: Names of regular meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) take zero article.

questions.prompt: He goes to ___ school five days a week.
questions.explanation: Institutions (school, hospital, church, prison) take zero article when referring to their primary institutional purpose.

questions.prompt: My favorite subject in high school was ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: Academic subjects and fields of study take no article.

questions.prompt: They play ___ tennis every Sunday morning.
questions.explanation: Sports and games take zero article.

questions.prompt: ___ honesty is the best policy.
questions.explanation: Abstract concepts used generally take no article.

questions.prompt: I will see you on ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: Days of the week, months, and holidays take zero article in general time expressions.

questions.prompt: She suffers from ___ insomnia.
questions.explanation: Most general medical conditions and illnesses take no article.

questions.prompt: Mount Everest is located in ___ Asia.
questions.explanation: Continents take zero article.

questions.prompt: ___ children need love and guidance.
questions.explanation: Plural nouns in generic contexts require zero article.

questions.prompt: He travels to work by ___ bus.
questions.explanation: Means of transportation preceded by 'by' take zero article (by bus, by car, by train).

questions.prompt: We celebrated ___ Christmas with our family.
questions.explanation: Holidays take zero article.

questions.prompt: She went to ___ hospital to visit her sick friend.
questions.explanation: Use 'the' because she is visiting a specific building/person, not receiving medical treatment as a patient.

questions.prompt: (British English) He was admitted to ___ hospital after the accident.
questions.explanation: In British/International English, 'in hospital' without an article refers to receiving medical care as a patient.

revision.reason: Longman lists 'be admitted to hospital' as British English and 'be admitted to the hospital' as American English. Marked the prompt as British English, as the explanation already states.

questions.prompt: ___ coffee that we bought in Colombia last year was excellent.
questions.explanation: Although 'coffee' is uncountable, it is specific here ('the coffee that we bought in Colombia last year'), so it takes 'the'.

revision.reason: Zero article was also acceptable for coffee grown in Colombia (a general category). Rewrote the prompt so the coffee is clearly specific.

questions.prompt: I love drinking ___ coffee in the morning.
questions.explanation: Refers to coffee in general, an uncountable noun, so no article is needed.

questions.prompt: ___ Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.
questions.explanation: Countries with words like 'Republic', 'Kingdom', or 'States' take 'the'.

questions.prompt: She has ___ European accent.
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with the consonant sound /j/, so it takes 'a'.

questions.prompt: He gave me ___ advice on my resume.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun and takes zero article when speaking generally.

questions.prompt: ___ United States is a global economic power.
questions.explanation: Plural country names and country names including 'States' take 'the'.

questions.prompt: We live on ___ Main Street.
questions.explanation: Street names generally take zero article.

questions.prompt: ___ Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.
questions.explanation: Oceans always take 'the'.

questions.prompt: He spent ___ hour reviewing his notes.
questions.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a silent 'h', starting with a vowel sound, requiring 'an'.

questions.prompt: I watched ___ movie you recommended.
questions.explanation: The movie is specified ('the movie you recommended'), taking 'the'.

questions.prompt: ___ music always relaxes me when I am stressed.
questions.explanation: Abstract/uncountable noun used in a general sense takes zero article.

questions.prompt: Did you like ___ music played at the concert?
questions.explanation: Specific music ('music played at the concert'), taking 'the'.

questions.prompt: She works as ___ nurse at the local clinic.
questions.explanation: Professions take 'a' or 'an' when stating someone's job.
